about: Born, Not Made, tail copy variant (23 Nov 2026): the parent prints the two segments of a new tail and puts a new arm together from four floating modules. Frame: x toward the parent's mouth, y port, z up, meters, origin on the tank floor; the parent sits 200 mm back from the quilted head simulator.

tank.name: Glasscages rimless 96 x 36 x 16 in (the fertile build's tank)

stages.name: The parent and the parts
stages.text: The parent, a hard tail with its DexArm and a quilted head, sits at the back of the tank. Four arm modules wait on a shelf hung on the front glass: base, upper arm, forearm, end effector, each in a sealed housing.

stages.name: Pods on the floor
stages.text: The holder lays N's two sealed pods on the floor of the bowl, the way it lays a kit: a battery and a Raspberry Pi in one, the pump in the other.

stages.name: Print N
stages.text: The needle prints the nose segment folded flat over the pods: 18 layers, 79 mm tall, double wall with the quilt between.

stages.name: Cure
stages.text: Dragon Skin 30 cures in the gel for 16 hours.

stages.name: Birth of N
stages.text: The holder lifts the folded nose out of the gel and pushes it over the lip. Outside, air goes into the quilt and the segment opens to its printed shape.

stages.name: N wakes
stages.text: The Pi in the pod boots on its own battery. N has the pump, so the first part of the child is the part that moves: it swims clear of the mouth.

stages.name: Print F
stages.text: The needle prints the face segment: a quilted ring with the arm's seat plate printed into its floor, 18 layers, 79 mm tall.

stages.name: Cure
stages.text: Sixteen hours in the gel.

stages.name: Birth of F
stages.text: F is born the same way. It has no pump: it opens in front of the mouth and waits.

stages.name: N moves F aside
stages.text: N pushes F against the port glass and parks itself against the starboard glass: the middle of the tank is clear.

stages.name: To the shelf
stages.text: The parent drives its whole body 948 mm, tail and head together, between the two parked halves, until its lower lip meets the shelf on the front glass.

stages.name: Module 1: base
stages.text: The base slides down the shelf to the middle. The holder's crank, the hook it uses at a birth, reaches 25 mm past the lip, catches the eye on the housing and draws it in over the lip. It goes down onto the gel floor of the bowl, the base plate toward the mouth.

stages.name: Module 2: upper arm
stages.text: The upper arm slides down the shelf to the middle. The holder's crank, the hook it uses at a birth, reaches 25 mm past the lip, catches the eye on the housing and draws it in over the lip. The upper arm goes down onto the shoulder: magnets pull the last 2 mm and a spring latch clicks.

stages.name: Module 3: forearm
stages.text: The forearm slides down the shelf to the middle. The holder's crank, the hook it uses at a birth, reaches 25 mm past the lip, catches the eye on the housing and draws it in over the lip. The forearm goes onto the elbow and clicks.

stages.name: Module 4: end effector
stages.text: The end effector slides down the shelf to the middle. The holder's crank, the hook it uses at a birth, reaches 25 mm past the lip, catches the eye on the housing and draws it in over the lip. The end effector clicks onto the wrist. The arm is whole, folded, lying in the gel.

stages.name: Back
stages.text: The parent drives back with the folded arm lying in its bowl.

stages.name: The folded arm
stages.text: Every joint is vertical while it lies like this, so every module went straight down onto the one before. Nothing was screwed.

stages.name: N docks to F
stages.text: N backs its open end onto F's rear cuff: magnets in the two cuffs, the same as the docking of a tail and a head. Pogo pads in the cuff carry the battery's power into F. The shell is whole, still without an arm.

stages.name: The shell docks on the mouth
stages.text: The shell swims round and brings its open face against the parent's mouth. Nine magnet pairs in F's cuff meet steel disks in the quilt round the mouth.

stages.name: Birth of the arm
stages.text: The parent vents its lower lip, which folds down flat on the floor; the gel stays, the water stands over it. The holder pushes the folded arm base first along the floor, out of the mouth into F: 110 mm, until the base plate hooks the hinge bar of the seat.

stages.name: The parent backs away
stages.text: The magnets of the face cuff let go. The arm is hooked in F, so the parent backs 305 mm away on its wheels; the holder carries the elbow end of the arm over the flat lip and sets it on the tank floor. The lip fills again.

stages.name: The arm stands up
stages.text: The seat's pogo pads touch the base plate: the arm has power for the first time. It presses its forearm on the floor and stands itself up about the hinge, and the seat magnets close.

stages.name: It looks
stages.text: It turns its base a little to one side and back, the first move it chooses.

stages.name: It unfolds
stages.text: The arm unfolds to its rest pose. The new tail is whole: N, F and an arm, and the parent kept its own.

stages.name: A tail of its own
stages.text: The new tail can dock to any head and print. Its two segments are quilted and soft where the parent's were printed hard on the H2S; its nose came out a little longer. Same principle, its own body.

notes: The tail splits where the hard tail is already printed in two on the H2S (x = -215 mm). Each half has less skin than a head (0.170 and 0.281 against 0.328 m2), so each folds into the head's own print envelope.

No floats. Each module has a closed, sealed housing that holds air, trimmed with a little steel so it weighs 0.04 to 0.10 N in water and sits still on the shelf. The parent's arm (500 g payload, a 2.45 N magnet) could not lift its own base in air (1.4 kg), but it can carry it under water. This is why the arm is put together under water, and why the water stands at 270 mm.

The modules wait on a shelf hung on the tank's front glass, at the height of the lower lip. The shelf slopes to its middle, so when one module is taken the next slides into place. The parent drives its whole body up to the shelf, takes the four modules in through the mouth and puts the arm together in its bowl, then drives back.
In the bowl the folded arm lies turned 33 deg so its elbow is not under the parent's own shoulder, where the DexArm cannot bend down (joint 1 does not lean back).
